title: Baked Mostaccioli with Sausage
seoTitle: Baked Mostaccioli with Sausage | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Cheesy mostaccioli with hot Italian sausage baked for ten
subtitle: Cheesy mostaccioli with hot Italian sausage baked for ten
description: Hot Italian sausage browns with garlic and marinara, tosses with par-cooked ziti and ricotta, then bakes under a mozzarella cap until golden and bubbling.

steps.title: Par-cook the pasta
steps.instruction: Boil ziti in salted water until just shy of al dente, about 8 minutes. Drain and toss with a teaspoon of oil.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.instruction: Cook sausage with garlic over medium-high heat 10 minutes, breaking into crumbles until browned. Stir in marinara and simmer 5 minutes.

steps.title: Mix the cheese layer
steps.instruction: Combine ricotta, half the mozzarella, Parmesan, egg, basil, and red pepper flakes until smooth.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.instruction: Toss ziti with sausage sauce, dollop ricotta mix throughout, top with remaining mozzarella. Cover and bake at 375°F 25 minutes, uncover and bake 15 more until golden. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes so cheese sets. Cut into ten portions and serve with extra marinara at the line.

proTips: Sweet Italian sausage works if your hall does not love heat—swap half and half.
A thin layer of sauce on the pan bottom prevents sticking on cleanup.
Freeze half a pan before baking for an emergency meal on a future shift.
tonightSpread: Baked ziti squares with garlic bread and simple Caesar salad.
Extra red pepper flakes and grated Parmesan at the table.
leftovers: Reheat covered at 350°F with splash of water to loosen sauce.
Pan-fry cold squares in oil for crispy-edged ziti bites.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Baked ziti is crew comfort math—cheap pasta, big flavor, one pan to scrub. It slices into portions for fast service and tastes even better as leftovers.
mealPrepNotes: Undercook ziti by 2 minutes—it finishes in the oven. Assemble in disposable pans for easy cleanup. Rest 10 minutes before cutting so layers set.
